title: Past Simple
tagline: finished actions at a finished time
why: We use the past simple to tell stories, talk about last weekend and describe our work history. It is the tense you use most when you talk about your life.
know: the spelling rules for regular verbs: worked, lived, stopped, studied
past time words: yesterday, last week, in 2019, two days ago
understand: why we say I didn't go, not I didn't went: did already shows the past
why a finished time (yesterday, last year) needs the past simple, not the present perfect
able: talk about your weekend, your last holiday or your last job
ask questions like Where did you go? and What did you buy?
make negative sentences with didn't + base verb
mistakes: I didn't went to work yesterday.
Did you saw the game last night?
Did you see the game last night?
I have visited Montreal last summer.
She buyed a new coat on Saturday.
She bought a new coat on Saturday.
use: a finished action at a finished time: I called my sister yesterday.
a list of actions in a story, one after another: I got up, had a shower and left.
a past habit or state that is now finished: We lived in Ottawa for six years.
form: I worked late. She went home. (regular verbs add -ed; irregular verbs change)
I didn't work late. She didn't go home. (didn't + base verb)
signals: yesterday, last night / week / year, two days ago, in 2015, on Monday, when I was a child, then, after that
tip: Use the past form only once. In questions and negatives, did carries the past, so the main verb goes back to the base form: She went but Did she go? and She didn't go.

pick.q: We ___ dinner at a Thai restaurant last Friday.
pick.why: 'Last Friday' is a finished time, so we use the past simple: had.

pick.q: I didn't ___ the email until this morning.
pick.why: After didn't we use the base verb: didn't see.

pick.q: ___ you remember to lock the door when you left?
pick.why: This is a question about a past action, so we use Did + base verb: Did you remember?
'In 1998' is a finished time, so we use the past simple: moved.

pick.q: Yesterday she ___ the bus because she got up late.
pick.why: 'Yesterday' is a finished time, so we use the past simple: missed.

pick.q: How much ___ your new phone cost?
pick.why: Past questions with a main verb use did: How much did it cost?

pick.q: They ___ very tired after the long drive.
pick.why: With they, the past of be is were: They were tired.

pick.q: Two years ago I ___ in a bank downtown.
pick.why: 'Two years ago' is a finished time, so we use the past simple: worked.

type.q: I ___ (buy) some bread on the way home last night.
type.why: Buy is irregular. The past simple is bought.
Negative past simple: didn't + base verb. We didn't watch.

type.q: He ___ (stop) the car at the red light and waited.
type.why: Stop ends in one vowel + one consonant, so we double the p: stopped.
Past question: did + subject + base verb. Where did you park?

type.q: My daughter ___ (study) nursing at college from 2018 to 2021.
type.why: Study ends in consonant + y, so y changes to i: studied.

type.q: I ___ (take) my mother to the doctor on Tuesday.
type.why: Take is irregular. The past simple is took.

type.q: The meeting ___ (not / start) on time last week.
type.why: Negative past simple: didn't + base verb. It didn't start.

type.q: Last winter we ___ (go) skiing in Quebec.
type.why: Go is irregular. The past simple is went.

spot.q: I didn't went to the party on Saturday.
spot.why: After didn't we use the base verb: I didn't go.

spot.q: Did you found your keys yesterday?
spot.why: After Did we use the base verb: Did you find?

spot.q: I have met my wife in 2005.
spot.why: 'In 2005' is a finished time, so we use the past simple: I met my wife in 2005.

spot.q: The children plaied outside all afternoon.
spot.why: Play ends in vowel + y, so we just add -ed: played.

spot.q: When you arrived at the hotel?
spot.why: Past questions need did + base verb: When did you arrive?

order.a: What did you do last weekend?
order.why: Question word + did + subject + base verb: What did you do?

order.a: I didn't sleep well last night.
alt: Last night I didn't sleep well.
order.why: Negative past simple: subject + didn't + base verb + time.

order.a: We left the office at six o'clock.
alt: At six o'clock we left the office.
order.why: Subject + past verb + object + time. Left is the past of leave.

order.a: Did your brother call you yesterday?
order.why: Past question: Did + subject + base verb: Did your brother call?

pick.q: I ___ my keys at work yesterday.
pick.why: 'Yesterday' is a finished time, so we use the past simple: forgot.

pick.q: We didn't ___ enough time to visit the museum.
pick.why: After didn't we use the base verb: didn't have.
A past question with a main verb uses did: What time did the train leave?

pick.q: The weather ___ terrible on our holiday.
pick.why: With a singular subject (the weather), the past of be is was.

pick.q: He ___ his job three months ago.
pick.why: 'Three months ago' is a finished time, so we use the past simple: lost.

pick.q: ___ you enjoy the concert last night?
pick.why: 'Last night' is past, so the question uses Did + base verb: Did you enjoy?

type.q: Last week she ___ (write) a long letter to her grandmother.
type.why: Write is irregular. The past simple is wrote.

type.q: I ___ (not / understand) the question at first.
type.why: Negative past simple: didn't + base verb. I didn't understand.

type.q: We ___ (plan) last year's trip very carefully.
type.why: Plan ends in one vowel + one consonant, so we double the n: planned.

type.q: What ___ (the doctor / say) about your back yesterday?
type.why: Past question: did + subject + base verb. What did the doctor say?

type.q: On Saturday they ___ (try) the new cafe on Queen Street.
type.why: Try ends in consonant + y, so y changes to i: tried.

type.q: I ___ (lose) my wallet on the subway last month.
type.why: Lose is irregular. The past simple is lost.

type.q: My son ___ (not / eat) his vegetables at dinner last night.
type.why: Negative past simple: didn't + base verb. He didn't eat.

type.q: Yesterday we ___ (arrive) at the airport two hours early.
type.why: Arrive ends in e, so we just add -d: arrived.

spot.q: My husband didn't liked the film.
spot.why: After didn't we use the base verb: didn't like.

spot.q: Did she told you about the party?
spot.why: After Did we use the base verb: Did she tell you?

spot.q: I have seen him at the supermarket yesterday.
spot.why: 'Yesterday' is a finished time, so we use the past simple: I saw him.

spot.q: We catched the last bus home.
spot.why: Catch is irregular. The past simple is caught.

order.a: Where did you buy that jacket?
order.why: Question word + did + subject + base verb: Where did you buy?

order.a: She didn't answer her phone this morning.
alt: This morning she didn't answer her phone.
order.why: Negative past simple: subject + didn't + base verb.

order.a: We spent two weeks in Halifax last summer.
alt: Last summer we spent two weeks in Halifax.
order.why: Subject + past verb + object + place + time. Spent is the past of spend.

bank.q: I ___ to the dentist last Thursday.
bank.why: 'Last Thursday' is a finished time, so we use the past simple: went.
After didn't we use the base verb: didn't know.

bank.q: ___ they win the game on Sunday?
bank.why: 'On Sunday' is past here, so we ask with Did + base verb: Did they win?

bank.q: Yesterday we ___ at home all day because of the snow.
bank.why: 'Yesterday' is a finished time, so we use the past simple: stayed.

bank.q: The shop ___ closed when we got there.
bank.why: With a singular subject (the shop), the past of be is was.
When who is the subject, we don't use did: Who gave you the flowers?

bank.q: I ___ my first car when I was twenty.
bank.why: 'When I was twenty' is a finished time, so we use the past simple: bought.
A past question with a main verb uses did: Why did you leave?
Drive is irregular. The past simple is drove.

bank.q: I ___ (not / feel) well yesterday, so I stayed home.
bank.why: Negative past simple: didn't + base verb. I didn't feel well.

bank.q: The baby ___ (cry) all night, so we didn't sleep.
bank.why: Cry ends in consonant + y, so y changes to i: cried.
Past question: did + subject + base verb. How did you get here?

bank.q: We ___ (shop) for groceries after work yesterday.
bank.why: Shop ends in one vowel + one consonant, so we double the p: shopped.

bank.q: They didn't came to the meeting.
bank.why: After didn't we use the base verb: didn't come.

bank.q: Did you spoke to the manager?
bank.why: After Did we use the base verb: Did you speak?

bank.q: I met an old friend downtown on Saturday.
bank.why: This sentence is correct. Met is the past of meet, and 'on Saturday' is a finished time.

bank.q: We didn't have time for lunch yesterday.
bank.why: This sentence is correct: didn't + base verb (have) for a finished time.

bank.a: What time did you get up today?
bank.why: Question word + did + subject + base verb: What time did you get up?

bank.a: I didn't hear the alarm this morning.
alt: This morning I didn't hear the alarm.
bank.why: Negative past simple: subject + didn't + base verb.

bank.a: We moved to Toronto five years ago.
alt: Five years ago we moved to Toronto.
bank.why: Subject + past verb + place + time. Ago comes after the time period.
